VO.sub: Did you know Pokémon was inspired by a little boy… catching bugs?
His name was Satoshi Tajiri.
Growing up near Tokyo, Satoshi spent his summers exploring the countryside, hunting for beetles and collecting insects.
He was so good at it, his friends called him "Doctor Bug." Which, honestly, is the coolest nickname a kid could ask for.
But as the city expanded, the forests and fields he loved began disappearing… and so did the bugs.
Years later, Satoshi discovered something fascinating.
Two Game Boys… connected by a cable.
And he imagined tiny creatures traveling between them!
What if children could collect, battle, and trade creatures… just like he once collected insects?
Together with his team at Game Freak, he spent six years bringing that idea to life.
Money got tight. VERY tight.
Satoshi stopped paying himself. Five members of the team quit.
The studio almost didn't make it.
Then, on February 27, 1996, Pokémon Red and Green were released in Japan.
But at first… sales were modest.
Then came a secret. Just before launch, programmer Shigeki Morimoto had sneaked one extra creature into the game, as a prank: Mew.
In 1996, CoroCoro Comic offered Mew to just 20 lucky readers… and more than 78,000 kids entered!
Suddenly, everybody wanted to know what else was hiding in the game. And sales took off.
And a childhood fascination became a worldwide phenomenon.
Today, more than 515 million Pokémon games have been sold.
Over 85 billion cards have been printed. That's about ten cards for every person on Earth. So… where are yours?
Pokémon is often called the highest-grossing media franchise in history. Bigger than Star Wars. Bigger than Mickey Mouse.
And some of those little pieces of cardboard… got very, VERY expensive.
In 1998, a Japanese magazine gave away a special Pikachu card as a prize for a drawing contest. Only 39 were ever handed out.
In 2021, YouTuber Logan Paul bought a perfect copy for about 5.3 million dollars.
In February 2026, he sold it… for 16.5 million.
A world record! For a prize from a drawing contest.
So if your mom threw out your old cards… maybe don't tell her what they're worth now.
And the story isn't over. A brand-new generation, Pokémon Winds and Waves, is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027.
Will the cards keep climbing? Could a childhood binder become a retirement plan? Nobody knows. Prices can crash just as fast as they soar.
But one thing's for sure: kids everywhere will keep exploring, collecting, and trading… just like Satoshi did.
All because one little boy… loved catching bugs.
